archetypes.name: scope-drift
archetypes.rationale: Plan body names files (implement-bootstrap.md, test-implement-timing-rehydration.md) absent from scope-files.txt — silent omissions cause post-merge follow-up churn.
archetypes.prompt_body: Cross-reference every file path named in the plan body against the declared scope-files list. Flag any file the plan says it will modify or create that does not appear in scope-files.txt, and any file in scope-files.txt that the plan body never mentions. Pay particular attention to documentation companion files (*.md siblings of *.sh scripts) and test-harness prose files, as these are the most commonly omitted from scope declarations. Verify that the plan's 'Files to modify/create' section is exhaustive and matches what the plan steps actually describe. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: helper-coupling
archetypes.rationale: Plan defines emit_plugin_root_env inside write-session-env.sh and says implement-bootstrap.sh calls it, but leaves the cross-script invocation mechanism unspecified — sourcing risks namespace pollution, duplication violates DRY.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine how the plan intends implement-bootstrap.sh to invoke emit_plugin_root_env, a function the plan defines inside write-session-env.sh. Check whether the plan proposes sourcing write-session-env.sh (which imports its entire namespace and executes its top-level code), duplicating the helper inline, or some other mechanism not stated. Verify that whichever approach the plan describes is consistent with how implement-bootstrap.sh currently invokes other helpers in scripts/ by checking its existing source or subprocess patterns. If the plan is silent on the invocation mechanism, flag it as an implementation gap. Also check that every new shell construct proposed for write-session-env.sh and implement-bootstrap.sh respects the Bash 3.2 portability constraint documented in BASH_AUTHORING.md. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: count-parity
archetypes.rationale: Plan makes conflicting numeric claims (description ~41, SKILL.md prose 43, plan body 40=37+3) that should be grep-verifiable against the actual file but are not reconciled.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every numeric claim the plan makes about fence counts, line numbers, and expected post-edit cardinalities. The issue description states ~41 byte-identical instances while the SKILL.md prose reportedly says 43; the plan breaks this into 40 executable sites (37 post-Step-0 + 3 pre-bootstrap) plus 1 prose example. Grep the actual skills/implement/SKILL.md for the opening line of the 4-line awk fence to determine the true count and check whether any split (40+1, 40+3, or another) is consistent with the file. Also verify that the 40 explicit line numbers listed in the plan actually correspond to the awk fence in the current file, since the plan itself acknowledges line numbers shift as edits are applied. Flag any discrepancy that could cause the implementer to miss a fence, duplicate a replacement, or edit the wrong line. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
